g.text: module: st = A st−1 + Bz zt + Ba at , zt+1 = W ReLU( C st )
H = num_frames = num_hist = 3 , in all 400 sampled configs
the window IS the model's memory
nothing older than zt−2 is in the graph
IIR – one state, a learned decay
the past enters with weight Ak , with no cutoff at all
INIT – near-identity and action-free, exactly as `additive` does it
a contraction is the only init decision here with no precedent among the FIR modes
0.9 and not 1.0: the FIR modes carry no state, so none of them could ever diverge
the CONTROL – matched to 384 parameters out of 738 048
both counts built at render time: LinearDynamicsPredictor, D = 384 , H = 3 , num_patches = 1
FIR against IIR is then the only real difference between the two arms
FIR: zt+1 = W ReLU( Σk Ak zt−k + B at )
IIR: zt+1 = W ReLU( C st ) , st = A st−1 + Bz zt + Ba at
the scan is T = num_hist steps long, the same length the FIR modes unroll
the link, the rollout and the planner all see the same interface
